sents.text: Step one.
Open Google Drive and create a new folder called workbench.
Inside it, make three more folders: data, for datasets; notebooks, for your work; and outputs, for results like charts and files.
Keeping things in the same place every time saves you hours later.
Step two.
Go to colab dot research dot google dot com, and create a new notebook.
Give it a sensible name, like lesson three setup.
Then, from the File menu, move it into your workbench notebooks folder.
Colab saves notebooks to your Drive as you work.
Step three.
Connect the notebook to your Drive.
Colab has a small built-in command for this, called drive dot mount.
When you run it, Google asks your permission.
Say yes, and your Drive appears as a folder the notebook can use.
The guided lab shows you exactly where to find it.
Now test it.
Write a short line of text into a file in your outputs folder.
Then, from the Runtime menu, disconnect and delete the runtime.
That's like switching the computer off and throwing it away.
Connect again, reconnect your Drive, and read the file back.
If it's still there, your workbench remembers.
Congratulations: that's the most important habit in this whole series.
